notes: Extracted from homepage analysis of https://www.perk.com/ (hero, benefits, solutions-by-persona, footer) with contrast set {Ramp machine-version artifact (rejected), Brex, Navan}. Theme: warm-neutral-plus-acid-accent fintech minimalism — differentiates from sibling styles (Brex: white + safety orange; Navan: cool lavender + violet serif).

criteria.name: Warm neutral ground
criteria.what_it_checks: Page and section backgrounds sit in the warm bone/putty/ecru family, never blue-white, cool gray, or pure white.
criteria.observable: Dominant page bg hex in the range E4E0D5..F0EEE8 (warm neutral, LCh hue 60-120°); secondary surfaces (cards, nav pill) 1-2 tonal steps darker within the same family; zero blue-white or rgb(255,255,255) content fields on the main page.

levels.label: On-brand
levels.descriptor: All major surfaces are warm bone/ecru with deliberate tonal layering between page -> card -> nav (elevation by tone, not shadow).

levels.label: Partial
levels.descriptor: Warm bg for some sections but breaks into pure white or cool gray in >25% of the page.

levels.label: Off-brand
levels.descriptor: Cool white or blue-white canvas throughout (Brex-style) or dark-mode dark trend.

criteria.generation_rule: Set page background to a warm bone/ecru around #E6E6E0; build nav/cards as the next 1-2 tonal steps of the same ramp; never use pure white as a section surface.
pitfalls: Adding drop shadows for elevation instead of tonal steps

criteria.name: Acid accent discipline
criteria.what_it_checks: One and only one high-chroma acidic accent, deployed strictly on action surfaces (primary CTA fills, announcement bar, the product-in-context card). Never used illustratively.
criteria.observable: Accent hue 85..115 hue-angle yellow-green (e.g. #BEE93A); accent coverage < 8% of hero pixels; accent appears ONLY on button fills, the announcement ribbon, and the physical/virtual product object inside imagery; zero gradients on the accent.

levels.label: On-brand
levels.descriptor: Single acid accent, flat, reserved for CTAs + announcement + one product object; every other surface neutral.

levels.label: Partial
levels.descriptor: Right accent hue but used for icons/tags/decoration, OR second high-chroma hue introduced at similar weight.

levels.label: Off-brand
levels.descriptor: Saturated corporate hue (blue/violet), multi-color gradient accents, or the neutral field is broken with colored section backgrounds.

criteria.generation_rule: Choose one acid accent (#BEE93A-class). Use it ONLY for: primary button fills, the top announcement ribbon, and the physical product card inside photography. Everywhere else stays neutral. No gradients on the accent.
pitfalls: Letting the accent drift into icons, illustrations, badges
Adding a gradient to 'modernize' the accent

criteria.name: Monumental sans display type
criteria.what_it_checks: Display headlines are heavy grotesque sans (never serif), tight-tracked, set at 60-100px+ / 8vw, sentence case with deliberate line-breaking.
criteria.observable: H1 font-family matches /grotesk|neue-haas|inter|general-sans|helvetica|archivo|space-grotesk|custom-spartan|OTSono/i and weight >= 500; lh 0.95-1.05; tracking -0.01 .. -0.03em; size >= 60px at 1200px+ viewport; zero serif at display sizes.

levels.label: On-brand
levels.descriptor: Bold neo-grotesque sans, ~80-100px hero, -0.02em tracking, sentence case, deliberate 2-3-line breaks.

levels.label: Partial
levels.descriptor: Sans display but weight/size/tracking timid (e.g. 40-48px, regular weight, default leading), or word-spaced/kerned commercially.

levels.label: Off-brand
levels.descriptor: Serif editorial display (Navan-Didot style), or monospace/brutalist type, or tiny-but-brutal.

criteria.generation_rule: Headline font = heavy neo-grotesque sans, weight 500-700, -0.02em tracking, 0.95-1.05 line-height, 72-100px at wide viewports, sentence case, 2-3 deliberate line breaks. No serif anywhere above body size.
pitfalls: Brutalist monospace that fights the acid-minimal register
evidence: computed: h1 fs=80px fw=500 lh=72px ff='OTSono, -apple-system,...'

criteria.name: One explicit CTA grammar
criteria.what_it_checks: Primary CTAs are acid-filled pill (radius 999px or close) with 16px+ label and ' ›' chevron baked in; secondaries are 1.5-2px near-black outlined pills with chevron affordance (or plain underlined text-CTAs); no rounded-rect CTAs, no naked text-only primary.
criteria.observable: Primary CTA: border-radius >= 24px, fill = accent lime, label color near-black, has ' ›' glyphally appended or icon-slot; secondary: same geometry with transparent fill + black border; footer-corners-everted: every visible primary button matches the grammar.

levels.label: On-brand
levels.descriptor: Pill primary with chevron, outline pill secondary, smaller underlined text-link tertiary; consistent everywhere.

levels.label: Partial
levels.descriptor: Right family but wrong radii (rounded-rect Brex-style 10-14px) or missing chevron semantics.

levels.label: Off-brand
levels.descriptor: Left-aligned form-input blocks with embedded CTA, floating sticker-buttons, glitter gradients, or no visible CTA grammar.

criteria.generation_rule: Primary CTA: pill (border-radius >= 999px or full-stadium), acid lime fill, near-black 16px semibold label ending in ' ›'. Secondary: same pill, transparent fill, 1.5-2px black border, ' ⌄' or ' ›' chevron. Tertiary: underlined near-black text with ' ›'. Never rounded-rect.
pitfalls: Mixing pill primary with square secondary

criteria.name: Product-as-imagery, hardware-in-scene
criteria.what_it_checks: Hero/feature imagery is product UI rendered inside real-world hardware photography (laptop + phone in frame, hands, real surfaces) — never lifestyle-people photos with floating UI cards (Navan), never CGI-rendered product scenes (Brex), never vector mockups.
criteria.observable: Hero contains device photography with screen content at naturalistic angle + lighting; device-body visible in at least one layer (laptop bezel + notch OR phone with Dynamic Island); no isolated illustration, no 3D-abstract scene, no stock lifestyle-human photo with fake-app-overlay.

levels.label: On-brand
levels.descriptor: Laptop + phone + accessory card layered in natural overlap, real surface shadows, no story-people, no 3D fantasia.

levels.label: Partial
levels.descriptor: Clean product UI mock in an idealized vector-frame, OR people with product but no physical-device shot.

levels.label: Off-brand
levels.descriptor: Lifestyle + floating-card collage (Navan), CGI glossy product scene (Brex), illustration-heavy, or abstract visual metaphor.

criteria.generation_rule: Hero imagery = photography of real hardware (laptop, phone) showing the real product UI; shows hands / surfaces where context helps; layers overlap naturally; no illustration, no 3D abstract scenes, no lifestyle actors with floating cards.
pitfalls: CGI product renders with architectural platforms (Brex)

criteria.name: Tonal card elevation, borderless construction
criteria.what_it_checks: Secondary content lives in flat, borderless cards whose elevation comes from a tonal step within the warm ramp (no border, no shadow, no glow) at radius 24-32px.
criteria.observable: Cards = same-hue darker neutral fill vs page bg (not hue-shift), border-width 0, box-shadow none, border-radius >= 24px.

levels.label: On-brand
levels.descriptor: All cards flat, tonal-step fill, no border, no shadow, radius consistent across page -> card -> button.

levels.label: Partial
levels.descriptor: Flat cards but with 1px borders, small shadow, or hero uses tonal cards but body sections revert to hairline-bordered modules.

levels.label: Off-brand
levels.descriptor: Glassmorphism, stroked modules, heavy drop shadows, neumorphic inner-relief.

criteria.generation_rule: Build every module as flat, borderless, shadowless cards: fill = page bg ramp +2-6 steps darker, radius 24-32px. Elevation is always by tone, never by line or shadow.

criteria.name: Typographic hierarchy: display -> gray body, no color noise
criteria.what_it_checks: Hierarchies are expressed by size + weight + warm-gray VALUE only; never by introducing more hues.
criteria.observable: Body copy uses a gray ~#6E6E68; eyebrow = small-caps, letterspaced gray; headline = near-black #14140F; zero colored headings or colored body copy anywhere on the page (except accent CTA labels and legal-severity error text).

levels.label: On-brand
levels.descriptor: All type is near-black -> mid-gray; hierarchy ladder = display -> section-eyebrow -> card-head -> body; zero hue in typography.

levels.label: Partial
levels.descriptor: Mostly monochrome type but one gradient word, or color-coded heading-per-benefit (quartet-icons is OK but headings-no).

levels.label: Off-brand
levels.descriptor: Colored headings, rainbow headlines, duotone photography, or bright-off-black-on-black trend.

criteria.generation_rule: Typography is near-black on warm-neutral, mid-gray for body, small-caps lsp-gray for eyebrows. Color lives in the accent and in pastel icon glyphs ONLY — never in headings, never in body copy, never in links beyond the announcement ribbon.
pitfalls: Gradient fill on a word of the H1
evidence: computed: h1 color rgb(20,20,15), body rgb(0,0,0)

criteria.name: Generous whitespace-with-gravitational-anchor
criteria.what_it_checks: Hero vertical negative space >= 35% of viewport; section-to-section pauses are explicit (~90-120px of background); the monstrous display type anchors the composition and the negative space points AT it.
criteria.observable: Viewport hero: text+cta occupies ~35-55% of first paint height; inter-section gaps compute to 5-8 times the base-grid unit (8*12=96px..8*15=120px); zero chevron-arrows-inside-canvas nudging the user to scroll.

levels.label: On-brand
levels.descriptor: Hero floats in a wide warm field; below-the-fold is signalled by content crop (device sliver), not by scroll-hint arrows or chevrons.

levels.label: Partial
levels.descriptor: Generous top whitespace but section pauses inconsistent or modules squeezed.

levels.label: Off-brand
levels.descriptor: Hero heading starts almost at the frame edge, no breathing room, OR chevron-scroll-hint / bouncy-arrow present.

criteria.generation_rule: Give the hero 100+ px vertical negative space above and below the display type; section-to-section breaks are explicit ~90-120px of the page background; below-fold is signalled only by content cropping.
pitfalls: Queues dense stacked modules with tiny gaps

criteria.name: Pastel icon taxonomy (functional, not decorative)
criteria.what_it_checks: Illustration is replaced by small, flat solid icons, each color-coded pastel (purple / coral / sky / rose) to label a category of value; icons never use the accent hue, never appear behind containers.
criteria.observable: Icons are flat unicase glyphs at ~28-40px, no container bg, no stroke, each in a distinct pastel (violet, coral, sky, rose); pastel colors appear only on icons and on tiny status-chips in product UI.

levels.label: On-brand
levels.descriptor: One icon per section, pastel-coded by category, zero illustration, zero 'hero-abstract-art'. pastel accents look intentional and never compete with lime CTA.

levels.label: Partial
levels.descriptor: Icons present but in container-chips or gradients, or 5+ pastel hues introduced (loses taxonomy).

levels.label: Off-brand
levels.descriptor: Heavy abstract illustration, 3D blob characters, LMS-style cartoon scenes, or icons share the lime accent hue (competes with CTA).

criteria.generation_rule: Iconography: small (~32px) flat solid pastel glyphs; one hue per categories-of-value; never inside filled chips; never gradient; pastel palette = violet/coral/sky/rose (NOT lime); no illustration beyond this.
pitfalls: Putting the icon on a colored chip background (multiplies the hue-plane)
Making icons lime like the CTA (all green = no grammar)
Adding an abstract editorial illustration 'for texture'

Theme_Tips_summary.theme: Warm minimalism + one acid action hue
tips: Page bg = warm bone #E6E6E0; never pure white.
One accent only: #BEE93A; CTA + announcement ribbon + product-in-scene.
CTA = pill (999px) with ' ›'; never rounded-rect, never gradient.
Imagery = hardware-showing-the-UI, never lifestyle people with cards.

Theme_Tips_summary.theme: Elevation by tone, not by shadow
tips: Cards are tonal steps of the page background, not hairline boxes.
Type hierarchy expressed by size + weight + gray-value only.
Section pauses = 90-120px of page background; no scroll-hint arrows.
Icons = pastel, flat, small, one hue per category.
